W3 covenant cap collapses on sprite fallback

findings.title: Assist route-glow path geometry computes from the UNCAPPED width while the drawn ribbon uses the capped one (flags-on path)
findings.detail: The glow's WIDTH rides link_width_capped, but its wire_path_compute call passes band_world (uncapped); wire_paths_compute (the drawn ribbon) passes the capped band. Where the clamp bites, glow and stroke follow different polylines. Flags-on only (7.5 ships OFF).
findings.recommended_fix: Thread the capped band into the glow's wire_path_compute call, matching wire_paths_compute.

findings.title: Flags-on fan path passes screen-px band where end_apex expects world-px; stub_w mixes units
findings.detail: end_apex adds band_w*0.5 to a world-px rim radius, but draw_bundles passes band (= link_width_capped * v.scale, screen px); stub_w = min(world, screen)*0.6 then draw_fan_stub scales it again. Correct at scale 1.0, wrong at any other zoom (fan only, flags-on, count>1).
findings.recommended_fix: Pass link_width_capped (world px, unscaled) to end_apex; make stub_w world-px consistently.

findings.title: Sprite-sheet fallback: puck bboxes zero -> sprite_puck_target 0 -> covenant cap 0 -> router-ended links draw zero-width
findings.detail: On the documented primitive-fallback path (load failure prints + continues), node_draw_size_world has no primitive branch (unlike puck_rim_world/building_foot_world which keep pre-7.1 constants), so cap = 0.5 x 0 = 0 for any bundle touching a router. The PR's deferred item ('ignores the rung tables') understates this.
findings.recommended_fix: Give node_draw_size_world the same primitive-fallback branch the wire-clearance helpers have.

findings.title: wire_path_test fixtures are the vacuous cap-0 class (sprites.ok=false)
findings.detail: test_view leaves the sheet unloaded, so link_width_capped returns 0 and wire_paths_compute is unit-exercised only at zero width; the direct wire_path_compute pins use the uncapped band_world basis. The de-vacuated-bbox fix landed in look_l1_test but not here. Real-width path geometry is covered only by palcheck's pixel legs.
findings.recommended_fix: Set real puck bboxes in wire_path_test's fixture (mirror look_l1_set_puck_bboxes) and add one capped-width pin.

findings.title: Covenant consumer reversion is unpinned (mutation-proven this round)
findings.detail: Round main reverted the crisis outline to band_world (uncapped): all 114 render tests AND palcheck stayed green. The M-legs pin the derivation, not its consumers (outline, halos, rider lattice, assist glow) — a one-line consumer reversion ships silently.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a consumer pin (e.g. assert the outline/halo width equals the capped stroke + margin on a clamped fixture).

findings.title: zoom directive parse-guard edges have no direct tests (happy path rides one golden)
findings.detail: Refined from the lens's 'zero coverage': demos/dublin_board.dem exercises the happy path end-to-end (golden green this round), but the NaN/out-of-band guard legs and the rung derivation from d.zoom have no direct unit test.
findings.recommended_fix: One harness unit test: NaN, 0.99, 4.01 rejected; a known z maps to the expected rung.

findings.title: camera_update -> zoom_rung wiring line untested
findings.detail: No app test asserts zoom_rung tracks cam_zoom through camera_update (grep: zero zoom_rung refs in pullback_test); palcheck and the harness set the rung DIRECTLY (view.odin:1104, run.odin:327), bypassing the wiring. A wiring regression would not fail unit tests.
findings.recommended_fix: Assert in pullback_test that a seed pullback / wheel zoom moves view.zoom_rung per zoom_rung_of.

findings.title: draw_bundles header still teaches the superseded 3.3 three-lane-stripe canon as current law
findings.detail: This diff retires the lane stripes (the laneless ruling supersedes 3.3), but the doc block above the new laneless code still presents the 2026-08-12 three-lane ruling in full — the exact confusion the next editor will inherit.
findings.recommended_fix: Rewrite the header for the laneless single-stroke law; move the 3.3 text to a superseded-history note.

findings.title: zoom_rung stored on View though derivable from zoom; three write sites must stay consistent
findings.detail: zoom_rung is a pure function of zoom (zoom_rung_of) yet is stored and set at three sites. Current sites are consistent (verified); the design leaves a drift trap for any future zoom path that bypasses camera_update. No actual drift found this round.
findings.recommended_fix: Either derive on read (zoom_rung_of at the 2-3 consumers) or pin a debug assert that stored == zoom_rung_of(zoom).

findings.title: band_width has zero callers; its ONE-definition doc names consumers that now derive from link_width_capped
findings.detail: The covenant migration moved every consumer to link_width_capped, stranding band_width and its doc ('the pipe strokes, the packet riders, the selection halo, and the crisis outline all derive from it' — now false).
findings.recommended_fix: Delete band_width or repoint the doc at link_width_capped.

findings.title: node_draw_size_world parallels the existing puck_rim_world/building_foot_world x2 without their fallback branches
findings.detail: For sprites-ok the new helper is exactly 2x the existing clearance helpers; it omits their primitive-fallback branches (the root of the cap-collapse warning). Three parallel node-size derivations now exist.
findings.recommended_fix: Derive node_draw_size_world from the existing helpers (2x) so the fallback handling lives in one place.

findings.title: Dusk dot radius doc says the building's live footprint; code uses the HOUSE footprint for all non-DC roles
findings.detail: foot := sprite_house_target with only a DC override, so biz (1.10) and campus (1.22) dusk rings ring at house size — slightly undersized vs their silhouettes; the PR's 'rides the building's LIVE footprint' overstates.
findings.recommended_fix: Use the per-role target (the same switch draw_building uses) or correct the doc to 'house/host footprint'.

findings.title: PR body carries a stale ±2px stroke-width tolerance; the shipped gate enforces ±1.0px
findings.detail: The swarm tightened 2.0 -> 1.0 (the body documents the tightening elsewhere), but the rung-by-rung pixel-truths section still says ±2px. Body-internal inconsistency only; the code is the tighter, correct gate.
findings.recommended_fix: Fix the body line to ±1.0px at the next docs touch.

findings.title: draw_bundles keeps its flow parameter but discards it every call (_ = flow)
findings.detail: The lane caps died with the lane stripes; the parameter survives with an explanatory comment. Dead signature surface.
findings.recommended_fix: Drop the parameter at the next signature-breaking touch (or keep with the comment, documented).

findings.title: count_exact's doc comment stranded above measure_color_run
findings.detail: The inserted measure_color_run doc continues directly after count_exact's stranded doc, leaving both stacked above measure_color_run's proc.
findings.recommended_fix: Move count_exact's doc back onto count_exact.

findings.title: Advisory test gate: CONCERNS
findings.detail: P0/P1 core paths are mutation-pinned (M1-M9; M3/M6/M8 re-run RED-then-GREEN by the round main) and pixel-gated (palcheck legs green in round-main's own run); the concerns are P2-level: guard-edge tests, the rung wiring line, consumer reversion pins, cap-0 wire fixtures. Overall well above 80% with the golden corpus.
findings.recommended_fix: Close the five named P2 gaps in a follow-up; none gate this merge.
